source.note: Scan without a text layer. National Senior Certificate paper (cover: NATIONAL SENIOR CERTIFICATE; running header: NSC). The PDF includes the cover (printed page 1), the instructions (page 2) and the information sheet (page 11); PDF page n = printed page n. The cover states that the question paper consists of 10 pages and 1 information sheet. Duration 3 hours as printed on the cover. Source file and hash are recorded in sources/maths/manifest.json.

extraction.method: manual transcription from 170 dpi page renders, checked at 400 dpi where needed

questions.text_md: $3x^{2}+5x=4$  (correct to TWO decimal places)
Solve for $x$ and $y$.
questions.notes: A sum of two squares equals zero, so $3x-y=0$ and $x-5=0$. No dedicated skill for the sum-of-squares argument; tagged with simultaneous linear equations.

questions.text_md: For which value of $k$ will the equation  $x^{2}+x=k$  have no real roots?

questions.stem_md: The following geometric sequence is given:  $10\,;\,5\,;\,2{,}5\,;\,1{,}25\,;\,\ldots$

questions.text_md: Calculate the value of the $5^{\text{th}}$ term, $T_{5}$, of this sequence.
Determine the $n^{\text{th}}$ term, $T_{n}$, in terms of $n$.
Explain why the infinite series  $10+5+2{,}5+1{,}25+\ldots$  converges.
Determine $S_{\infty}-S_{n}$ in the form $ab^{n}$, where $S_{n}$ is the sum of the first $n$ terms of the sequence.
Determine the general term of the series in the form $T_{k}=bk+c$.
Write $S_{n}$ in sigma notation.
Show that  $S_{n}=4n^{2}-7n$.
Write down a numerical expression for $\mathrm{Q}_{6}$.
Calculate the value of $\mathrm{Q}_{129}$.
questions.notes: "value" is underlined in the paper. $\mathrm{Q}_{n}=-6+S_{n-1}$ of the series in the stem of QUESTION 3.

questions.text_md: Write down the equation of the asymptote of $f$.
Sketch the graph of $f$. Clearly indicate ALL intercepts with the axes as well as the asymptote.
The graph of $g$ is obtained by reflecting the graph of $f$ in the $y$-axis. Write down the equation of $g$.

questions.stem_md: Given:  $h(x)=2x-3$  for  $-2\leq x\leq 4$. The $x$-intercept of $h$ is Q.

questions.text_md: Determine the coordinates of Q.
Write down the domain of $h^{-1}$.
Sketch the graph of $h^{-1}$ in your ANSWER BOOK, clearly indicating the $y$-intercept and the end points.
For which value(s) of $x$ will $h(x)=h^{-1}(x)$?
$\mathrm{P}(x\,;\,y)$ is the point on the graph of $h$ that is closest to the origin. Calculate the distance OP.
questions.notes: OP is perpendicular to $h$ (shown dashed in the figure). Analytical-geometry skills used inside a P1 functions question.

questions.stem_md: Given:  $h(x)=f'(x)$  where $f$ is a function defined for  $-2\leq x\leq 4$.

questions.text_md: Explain why $f$ has a local minimum.
Write down the value of the maximum gradient of the tangent to the graph of $f$.

questions.stem_md:
The graphs of  $f(x)=-2x^{2}+18$  and  $g(x)=ax^{2}+bx+c$  are sketched below.

Points P and Q are the $x$-intercepts of $f$. Points Q and R are the $x$-intercepts of $g$. S is the turning point of $g$. T is the $y$-intercept of both $f$ and $g$.

questions.text_md: Write down the coordinates of T.
Determine the coordinates of Q.
Given that $x=4{,}5$ at S, determine the coordinates of R.
Determine the value(s) of $x$ for which $g''(x)>0$.
questions.notes: Needs the sign of $a$ in $g$ (from the graph or from finding $g$); $g''(x)=2a$ is constant.

questions.stem_md:
The function defined as  $y=\dfrac{a}{x+p}+q$  has the following properties:

- The domain is  $x\in R$, $x\neq -2$.
- $y=x+6$  is an axis of symmetry.
- The function is increasing for all  $x\in R$, $x\neq -2$.
questions.text_md: Draw a neat sketch graph of this function. Your sketch must include the asymptotes, if any.

questions.stem_md: The graph of $f$ shows the book value of a vehicle $x$ years after the time Joe bought it. The graph of $g$ shows the cost price of a similar new vehicle $x$ years later.

questions.text_md: How much did Joe pay for the vehicle?
Use the reducing-balance method to calculate the percentage annual rate of depreciation of the vehicle that Joe bought.
If the average rate of the price increase of the vehicle is $8{,}1\%$ p.a., calculate the value of $a$.

questions.stem_md: A vehicle that costs R450 000 now, is to be replaced at the end of 4 years. The old vehicle will be used as a trade-in. A sinking fund is created to cover the replacement cost of this vehicle. Payments will be made at the end of each month. The first payment will be made at the end of the $13^{\text{th}}$ month and the last payment will be made at the end of the $48^{\text{th}}$ month. The sinking fund earns interest at a rate of $6{,}2\%$ p.a., compounded monthly.
questions.text_md: Calculate the monthly payment to the fund.
questions.notes: Replacement cost = $a$ (QUESTION 7.3) less the trade-in value R243 736,90 (Q on the graph); 36 payments from month 13 to month 48.

questions.text_md: If  $f(x)=x^{2}-3x$, determine $f'(x)$ from first principles.
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}$  if  $y=\left(x^{2}-\dfrac{1}{x^{2}}\right)^{2}$
$D_{x}\left(\dfrac{x^{3}-1}{x-1}\right)$

questions.stem_md: Given:  $h(x)=-x^{3}+ax^{2}+bx$  and  $g(x)=-12x$. P and $\mathrm{Q}(2\,;\,10)$ are the turning points of $h$. The graph of $h$ passes through the origin.

questions.text_md: Show that  $a=\dfrac{3}{2}$  and  $b=6$.
Calculate the average gradient of $h$ between P and Q, if it is given that $x=-1$ at P.
questions.notes: No dedicated average-gradient skill; tagged with the gradient formula (average gradient = gradient of the chord PQ).

questions.text_md: Show that the concavity of $h$ changes at  $x=\dfrac{1}{2}$.
Explain the significance of the change in QUESTION 9.3 with respect to $h$.
Determine the value of $x$, given $x<0$, at which the tangent to $h$ is parallel to $g$.

questions.stem_md:
A rain gauge is in the shape of a cone. Water flows into the gauge. The height of the water is $h$ cm when the radius is $r$ cm. The angle between the cone edge and the radius is $60^{\circ}$, as shown in the diagram below.

Formulae for volume:  $V=\pi r^{2}h$;  $V=\dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^{2}h$;  $V=lbh$;  $V=\dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}$
questions.notes: The formulae for volume are printed in a box next to the diagram.

questions.text_md: Determine $r$ in terms of $h$. Leave your answer in surd form.
Determine the derivative of the volume of water with respect to $h$ when $h$ is equal to $9$ cm.

questions.stem_md:
For two events, A and B, it is given that:

$\mathrm{P(A)}=0{,}2$

$\mathrm{P(B)}=0{,}63$

$\mathrm{P(A\ and\ B)}=0{,}126$
questions.text_md: Are the events, A and B, independent? Justify your answer with appropriate calculations.

questions.stem_md: The letters of the word DECIMAL are randomly arranged into a new 'word', also consisting of seven letters. How many different arrangements are possible if:

questions.text_md: Letters may be repeated
Letters may not be repeated
The arrangements must start with a vowel and end in a consonant and no repetition of letters is allowed

questions.stem_md: There are $t$ orange balls and 2 yellow balls in a bag. Craig randomly selects one ball from the bag, records his choice and returns the ball to the bag. He then randomly selects a second ball from the bag, records his choice and returns it to bag. It is known that the probability that Craig will select two balls of the same colour from the bag is $52\%$.
questions.text_md: Calculate how many orange balls are in the bag.

figures.caption: Straight line h(x) = 2x - 3 for -2 <= x <= 4 with x-intercept Q, y-intercept -3 and the point P(x ; y) on h closest to the origin.
figures.notes: End points shown as solid dots, joined to the x-axis at -2 and 4 by dashed lines. P is the foot of the perpendicular from O to h.

figures.caption: Parabolas f(x) = -2x^2 + 18 and g(x) = ax^2 + bx + c sharing y-intercept T; f cuts the x-axis at P and Q, g at Q and R, with turning point S.
figures.notes: g is not given in the paper; x^2 - 9x + 18 follows from T(0 ; 18), Q(3 ; 0) and x = 4,5 at S (QUESTION 6.1.3).

figures.caption: Book value f (decreasing) and cost price g (increasing) of a vehicle against time in years, both starting at 450 000; T(4 ; a) on g and Q(4 ; R243 736,90) on f.
figures.notes: Rates are derived: f uses the reducing-balance rate from QUESTION 7.2 and g the 8,1% p.a. growth from QUESTION 7.3. Not to scale.

figures.caption: Inverted cone rain gauge with water at height h and radius r; the angle between the cone edge and the radius is 60 degrees. A box beside it lists volume formulae.

relations: angle between the cone edge and the radius = 60°
axis perpendicular to the water-surface radius
spec.animation_hint: water level rises in the cone; show r and V changing with h
